answer: Copernicus estimated that 2024’s global average temperature was 1.60°C above pre-industrial levels (1850–1900). The WMO’s consolidated estimate from six datasets was 1.55°C, with an uncertainty margin of ±0.13°C. These are estimates from different datasets and methods. A single year above 1.5°C does not mean the Paris Agreement’s long-term temperature threshold has been crossed, which is assessed over decades. [1][2]
raw_answer: Copernicus estimated that 2024’s global average temperature was **1.60°C above pre-industrial levels** (1850–1900). The WMO’s consolidated estimate from six datasets was **1.55°C**, with an uncertainty margin of ±0.13°C. These are estimates from different datasets and methods. A single year above 1.5°C does not mean the Paris Agreement’s long-term temperature threshold has been crossed, which is assessed over decades. [Copernicus / WMO]
